subject: QueryNest SDK: proposal for LlamaIndex adapter + lightweight tracing
messages:
From: Lina Zhou <lina@querynest.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QueryNest SDK: proposal for LlamaIndex adapter + lightweight tracing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the intro at the integrations summit — Omar and I had a good conversation with Vanessa afterwards and we think theres an opportunity to build a first-party adapter that makes QueryNest queries plug straight into LlamaIndex and Redwoods trace pipeline.

Quick summary of what we propose (attached PDF + diagram):
- LlamaIndex adapter: small shim that converts QueryNest search results into LlamaIndex Nodes and supports batched embedding lookups.
- Lightweight tracing: emit a compact trace envelope for each user query with timing, cache-hit flag, model-version and token-cost estimate (wed like Redwood to ingest these traces into your console for per-route cost attribution).
- Compatibility: support both Redwood-hosted and Dedicated customers via feature-flagged telemetry endpoints.

Were aiming for a pilot with one mutual customer in Q3. Ask: can you confirm whether Redwood would accept the trace envelope format in the attached diagram, and would you be open to a short spike where your SDK team does a 1-day review of our adapter implementation?

Attachments: querynest_sdk_proposal_v1.pdf, adapter_sequence_diagram.png

Cheers,
Lina Zhou
Head of Integrations, QueryNest
Lina@querynest.com
+1 (415) 555-0129

On Thu, Apr 29, 2027 at 08:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Lina — looping in our SDK and partnerships leads so we can scope the spike.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lina Zhou <lina@querynest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QueryNest SDK: proposal for LlamaIndex adapter + lightweight tracing

Hi Lina — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear proposal. Looping in Marissa (ISV programs) and Vanessa (partnerships) to coordinate product review and a pilot timeline.

Initial answers up-front:
- Tracing: the envelope you show looks reasonable; wed want a compact JSON schema (2-3kb max per trace) and a stable field for model_variant so our console can roll up costs.
- Pilot: 1-day spike from our SDK team to review the shim + sequence diagram is feasible. If the spike is positive, we can commit to a 6-week co-build for a hardened adapter with docs.

Questions for Lina/Omar:
1) Which mutual customer did you have in mind for the pilot? (well need a contact and expected query velocity)
2) Will QueryNest maintain the adapter repo or do you expect joint ownership?
3) Are there any privacy/data retention constraints we should bake into tracing (PII redaction, retention TTL)?

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a 45-min technical sync the week of May 3rd (we can bring an engineer to do an on-the-spot review).
- Share a short spike checklist (code pointers and acceptance criteria).

Marissa/Vanessa — any constraints from the ISV program side we should consider (certification steps, legal intake for telemetry endpoints)?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Developer Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: QueryNest SDK: proposal for LlamaIndex adapter + lightweight tracing

Karthik / Vanessa — forwarding QueryNests note with a few comments from the ISV side after a quick read.

Observations / proposed gating:
- Certification: well want an "interop checklist" itemizing: authentication (API key / OAuth options), telemetry opt-in, and an automated test that runs against a staging Redwood instance.
- Security/compliance: QueryNest will need to complete our standard vendor security questionnaire if the pilot uses customer data. We can provision an NDA+VSA if they prefer.
- Marketplace: long term, wed list the adapter in the ISV catalog; for that we require docs, a minimal CLI install, and a demo app.

Action items I can own:
- Draft a short spike checklist (1 page) and a basic certification checklist.
- Start a vendor security intake and share the questionnaire link (if they confirm pilot customer).

Karthik: can you triage the technical sync and propose 2 time slots? Lina/Omar: please reply with the mutual customer details and whether QueryNest prefers to keep the adapter repo under their org or as a joint repo.

Thanks — Marissa
Sr. Partner Programs Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Omar Reyes <omar@querynest.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QueryNest SDK: proposal for LlamaIndex adapter + lightweight tracing

Thanks all — quick answers below and were happy to take the next steps.

Mutual customer: CompassAI (contact: Priya Rao, priya@compassai.ai). Expected QPS: ~12 peak, mostly short recall queries.
Repo ownership: QueryNest prefers to own the repo initially (we have established CI + release cadence) but were open to adding Redwood as a collaborator and moving to a joint repo post-pilot.
Data/PII: for the pilot we will not include user PII in traces; retention TTL: 30 days. We can provide a redaction step in the adapter.

We are available for a 45-min technical sync on May 4th at 10:00am PT or May 5th at 1:00pm PT — Karthik, which works for your SDK engineer?

Attachments: data_flow_stub.csv

Best,
